newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sends mediator to mideast for talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sends mediator to mideast for talks.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday it would seek to build on a flurry of Middle East diplomatic activity by dispatching envoy Dennis Ross to the region for high level talks on advancing the peace process.
Ross is to go on Wednesday and deliver fresh U.S. proposals to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinan President Yasser Arafat, the White House said.

"The United States is prepared to do everything it can to ensure that the peace process continues on a sound and durable basis," spokesman Mike McCurry said in a statement. "In that spirit, Ambassador Ross will be conveying some U.S. ideas."

In an interview with CNN, Ross declined to specify the nature of the U.S. initiatives. He said the two sides needed first to focus on interim issues such as joint security measures then move to work on a broader settlement.

"The last thing that has to happen is we have to find a way to resume the permanent status talks, so that we can move ahead and begin to deal with what are some of the most difficult issues in the conflict," Ross said.
There has been a revival of diplomatic activity surrounding the Middle East peace process after Israel suspended plans for a new Jewish enclave in Arab East Jerusalem.
Israelis and Palestinians on Monday announced the partial resumption of their talks which had been deadlocked for four months, which the White House called "a step in the right direction."
The two sides have only agreed to talk about the list of mutual promises already made and not kept.

Israel has accused the Palestinians of breaching promises to control violence against the Jewish state while Palestinians opposed Israeli efforts to build new settlements in Arab East Jerusalem, arguing this contravened the 1993 Oslo peace accords.
"In recent weeks, the United States, in close cooperation with Egypt, has been working with Israelis and Palestinians on ways to move the process forward," the White House statement said.
Ross was scheduled to brief President Bill Clinton and Secretary of State Madeleine Albright upon his return this weekend, the White House said.
Syrian President Hafez al-Assad said in Damascus on Tuesday he could see no hope for Middle East peace despite the renewed diplomatic activity.
"It is difficult for me to say there is hope in light of the current situation," Assad said at a joint news conference with visiting Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.
"I don't think there is anyone who knows what is happening and could say there is hope ... everyday we get a new proof that there is no hope," the Syrian leader said.
